back: $H_{ij}=\partial^2f/\partial x_i\partial x_j$, an $(n,n)$ symmetric matrix of curvatures (mixed partials commute).
Eigenvalues of $H$: all $>0$ minimum; all $<0$ maximum; mixed signs saddle; zeros inconclusive.

front: Why eigenvalues and not the diagonal?
back: $\boldsymbol\delta^\top H\boldsymbol\delta=\sum\lambda_ic_i^2$ in the eigenbasis. $x^2+3xy+y^2$ has eigenvalues $5,-1$: a saddle.
$\theta\mathbf x+(1-\theta)\mathbf y\in C$ for all $\mathbf x,\mathbf y\in C$, $\theta\in[0,1]$: segments stay inside.
$f(\theta\mathbf x+(1-\theta)\mathbf y)\le\theta f(\mathbf x)+(1-\theta)f(\mathbf y)$: the chord lies above the graph.
$f(\mathbf y)\ge f(\mathbf x)+\nabla f(\mathbf x)^\top(\mathbf y-\mathbf x)$: the graph lies above every tangent plane.
$H(\mathbf x)\succeq0$ for every $\mathbf x$ in the (convex) domain; in 1-D, $f''\ge0$.
$\alpha f_1+\beta f_2$ with $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ is convex; so convex loss + ridge or lasso penalty stays convex.
Every local minimum is a global minimum; a stationary point is a global minimum. Gradient descent cannot be trapped.
$\mathbf x\leftarrow\mathbf x-H^{-1}\nabla f$, i.e. solve $H\boldsymbol\delta=-\nabla f$. Exact on quadratics, quadratic convergence near a minimum, $O(n^2)$ memory and $O(n^3)$ time.
$\mathcal L=f+\lambda g$; stationarity $\nabla f=-\lambda\nabla g$ plus $g=0$ ($n+1$ equations, $n+1$ unknowns).

front: Why are $\nabla f$ and $\nabla g$ parallel at a constrained optimum?
back: $\nabla g$ is normal to the constraint surface; $\nabla f$ must also be normal, else sliding along the surface would improve $f$.
Multipliers $\lambda_i\ge0$; complementary slackness $\lambda_ig_i=0$ (active constraint or zero multiplier).
$D(\boldsymbol\lambda)=\min_{\mathbf x}\mathcal L$ is concave and lower-bounds the primal optimum; for convex problems the maximum of $D$ equals the primal optimum (strong duality).
